counterevidence_and_alternatives: Historical budgets are below $1 million per year but cannot refute a later replacement quote with different scope.

City provided land and proposed capital/operations funding; documents recognize volunteer labor and in-kind matching contributions. This constrains a blanket claim that community self-help is prohibited.

Grantee/subcontractor arrangements are contemplated. Split community maintenance and specialist case/crisis services could be tested with comparable priced proposals; eligibility, approval, savings and staffing capacity remain unverified.
Some formal requirements address habitability, emergency response and accountability; their existence does not establish necessity, proportionality or observed effectiveness.
The opening-announcement stream and developer page do not verify current staffing, occupancy or executed agreements.

findings.claim: November2024 report says City staff required an operational service-provider agreement for the permit. It does not identify the imposing staff member, precise legal/permit basis, or whether an eligible community operator could qualify.

TVS selected/appointed Hope as exclusive operations agent. The supportive-services contract assigns management plus case coordination,24hour emergency response and three days per week on-site casework; it does not state a$1million annual fee.

Nov2024 report requested an agreement with TVS; Jan2025 report requested the funding contract with Hope. April2026 grant materials name Hope as City grantee and TVS as subcontractor. This verifies proposed funding custody, not cash transferred or a current irrevocable lock.

April2026 staff attributed the previous grant agreement expiring before execution to obtaining required insurance, and stated all required insurance was then in place. This is dated staff attribution, not proof of the present replacement-price cause.

The$300000City contribution is split into$103000capital and$197000operating reimbursement. Invoices must substantiate eligible costs, hours and rates. Remaining funds and unspent advances return to City; the attachment does not establish actual payments, TVS cash balance or an automatically portable award.

April report seeks Apr1 2026–Dec31 2027; attachmentcover/§1.2 say Mar1 2026–Feb28 2027; reporting/close-out period is Apr1 2026–Mar31 2027. ExhibitA describes calendar2026startup but ExhibitB labels calendar2025. Executed controlling version remains unknown.

No qualifying dated replacement-operator quote, termination notice, current signed operating agreement, current paid invoice or verified occupancy count was located within this bounded pass. Absence from this search does not show absence of these records. The roughly$1million annual replacement-price barrier remains the user-reported lead.
findings.locator: search scope/log and user task clarification

findings.claim: Historical services contract needs TVS consent for assignment/subcontracting and both parties signatures for amendment. Convenience termination clause literally says thirty(60)days, an unresolved wording mismatch. Proposed City budget changes need grantee written request and City Project Manager approval within the cap; other grant amendments/waivers need written authorized signatures.

Routing reimbursement through an operator can make community-built facilities depend on that operator or an approved funding change, even when the physical homes exist. Current cash availability, grant transferability and whether this is the operative bottleneck need records; neither theft nor justified pricing follows from the structure.
